posts.content:
🚨 CRITICAL: React Server Components have another unauthenticated Remote Code Execution vulnerability. And there's already a public PoC.

CVE-2026-126187 carries a CVSS 4.0 score of 9.5 and exposes vulnerable React Server Components implementations to remote code execution without authentication.

The exploit chain is particularly interesting:

🔴 Abuses a desynchronization bug in React Flight serialization.
🔴 Exploits detached ArrayBuffer views and incorrect length framing.
🔴 Turns a deserialization over-read into Server Action invocation.
🔴 Works through a crafted HTTP GET request, without requiring a multipart POST or Next-Action header.
🔴 Public PoC includes a reproducible Docker lab.
The scale is concerning. According to the November 11 npm data cited in the research, 73% of react-server-dom-webpack downloads were still using affected versions.

And here's the catch for Next.js developers: updating react and react-dom alone does not necessarily fix the vulnerable React Flight runtime bundled inside Next.js.
Fixed releases include React 19.0.9, 19.1.10 and 19.2.9, with Next.js fixes in 16.4.1 and 15.5.28.
No workaround is available. Upgrade now.

Full technical breakdown:
https://thecybersecguru.com/exploits/cve-2026-126187-react-flight-rce/

CVE-2026-59163.description: Mnemosyne is a memory layer for artificial intelligence agents. Prior to v3.10.1, the auth check in mnemosyne/core/sync_server.py parsed the JWT's header and payload using base64 decoding, then passed the token to a jwt library call with options that effectively disabled signature verification. The server accepted any well-formed token regardless of the signature, including tokens with alg: none and tokens signed with the wrong key. The fix in v3.10.1 replaces the broken decode with a from-scratch HS256 verifier using only the Python standard library. For users who cannot upgrade immediately, restrict network access to the sync server endpoint to trusted clients only. Firewall, reverse proxy with mTLS, or localhost bind with SSH tunnel are all viable. The vulnerability is not exploitable against an unreachable endpoint.

🚨 A VISIT TO A MALICIOUS WEBSITE COULD GIVE ATTACKERS REMOTE CODE EXECUTION ON YOUR MACHINE.

Technical breakdown, affected versions, attack mechanics and mitigation:
https://thecybersecguru.com/news/fortinet2shell-cve-2026-121529/

Fortinet2Shell (CVE-2026-121529) is a newly disclosed critical vulnerability affecting Fortinet FortiClient, with a CVSS score of 9.1.

The attack chain is particularly concerning because a malicious website sends cross-origin requests to a privileged local FortiClient service. Due to a CORS / origin validation failure, attackers can abuse that service to execute arbitrary code on the victim's endpoint.

No authentication required. No special privileges required. Just one visit to a malicious webpage.

The vulnerability affects FortiClient for Windows, macOS and Windows PAM across specific 7.2 and 7.4 releases.

Some important details for defenders:

• Tracked as CVE-2026-121529 (CWE-346).
• Discovered by Kevin Joensen of Baldur Security.
• Windows hunting indicators include TCP port 9191 and FortiVRS.exe.
• Fixed releases include FortiClient 7.4.8 and 7.2.15.
• No virtual patch is available.

This is another reminder that local services exposed by endpoint security software can become an attack surface themselves.

new `git` CVE just dropped: might be good for @forgejo and @Codeberg to publish a statement

https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/cve-2026-105437

CVE-2026-105437.description:
Affected versions of Git have a heap buffer overflow in the three-way merge
code (xdiff), which an attacker can trigger through a repository they
control.

When Git merges a file, it first adds up the size of the merged
output, allocates a buffer of that size, and then writes the output into
it. That total was kept in a 32-bit signed integer. The
conflict-marker-size attribute, which can be set from a committed
.gitattributes file, accepts any positive integer, and the markers are
written several times for every conflict. A small file with a huge marker
size and many separate conflicts can therefore push the total past 4 GiB,
so the integer wraps to a small value and Git writes attacker-controlled
merge output past the end of a buffer that is too small. At minimum this
crashes Git, and because the overflow is large and its contents are largely
attacker-controlled, worse heap corruption is possible.

Any command that does a textual three-way merge can trigger it, such
as git-merge(1), git-rebase(1), git-cherry-pick(1), and
git-merge-tree(1). The latter is most likely a target for Git forges,
which might use git-merge-tree(1) on the server-side to check
mergeability. When the server reads attributes from trees in the
repository (for example through attr.tree or --attr-source), any
user who can push branches and request that they be merged (for
example by opening a pull or merge request) can trigger the overflow
without anyone else doing anything, and the data they push is small
because the oversized output only appears during the merge.

The problem has been patched by computing the size as size_t and
checking every addition for overflow, so Git stops with an error
instead of overflowing.

Servers that cannot upgrade right away can add

* conflict-marker-size=7

to each repository's info/attributes as a workaround, which overrides
any in-tree .gitattributes, or turn off server-side mergeability checks for
untrusted repositories.

CVE-2026-126617.description: SQL injection in the database layer of Progressive Robot hMailServer 6.0.0-B1 through 6.2.18, when the server uses MySQL/MariaDB or PostgreSQL, allows a remote attacker to alter SQL statements the server runs. On those two engines parameters are not bound: SQLStatement::GenerateFromCommand wrote each value into the statement's text as a quoted literal with a separate string replacement over the whole text per parameter, so a value holding the name of a parameter substituted after it had that name replaced, inside the value, by the later value with its own quotes, which ended the literal early and placed the later value in the statement as SQL. The row the server writes for each recipient of a queued message carries the recipient's address twice, so in the default configuration an authenticated user who may send mail reaches it by sending to an address of their choosing. A remote unauthenticated sender reaches the same statement through a message the server sends to the envelope sender, such as a delivery failure notice or an automatic reply, and, when greylisting or message indexing is enabled (both are off by default), through the greylisting record's envelope addresses or through the message metadata the server stores for IMAP SORT, which carries four header fields of a received message. An altered statement runs with the privileges of the server's database account; on PostgreSQL, whose client call runs every statement in the text it is given, further statements can follow it, while on MySQL/MariaDB, where one statement is run per call, the change is confined to the statement it is in. SQL Server and SQL Server Compact, where parameters are bound, are not affected.

CVE-2026-126613.description: Allocation of resources without limits in the JSON reader of Progressive Robot hMailServer 6.3.2 through 6.3.7 allows a remote attacker to exhaust the server's memory and hold its threads, making mail delivery, the REST API and the webmail unavailable. The reader built a tree of values far larger than the text it read, copying each value into every level above it, and set no bound on the number of values, so a single JSON document of many small values, within the 16 MB the server reads, raised the service's memory by about 2 GB and held one thread for seconds to minutes. From 6.3.4 a remote unauthenticated attacker reaches the reader by mailing such a document as a TLS-RPT report, up to 16 MB once decompressed, to a hosted domain's report mailbox, where an administrator has set one; it is read on a mail delivery thread (ten by default), and those threads deliver all mail, local and outbound. From 6.3.4 it is also reached without an account through the reply to a password-protected message, with the message's link alone, where the REST API is on (it is off by default) and a public base URL for such links is set; and by any account, from 6.3.2 through the webmail's send and draft routes and from 6.3.4 through its other routes granted 16 MB and the send API; the webmail's send, draft and settings routes parsed the body again for each member read. The REST API serves every request on four worker threads, in the process that also serves SMTP, IMAP and POP3, so a few such documents at once make it unavailable and can exhaust the machine's memory and end the whole service. This is a separate defect from CVE-2026-107574, the reader's handling of duplicate member names, fixed in 6.3.6.

CVE-2026-126621.description: Progressive Robot hMailServer 6.0.0-B1 through 6.3.7 on Windows hands OpenSSL the names of its own TLS files - the listeners' certificates, chains, private keys and Diffie-Hellman parameters, a port's client-certificate CA file (from 6.2.19), the object store's CA file (from 6.3.4) and the ACME client's keys and certificates - as Latin-1 bytes, which on code page 1252 are the code page's own for U+00A0 to U+00FF, and OpenSSL's file opening on Windows reads a name as UTF-8 first and opens the file at that reading when it is there, or creates it there when its folder is. When every byte of a configured name outside ASCII also reads as UTF-8 - for example U+00C3 U+00A9, the bytes C3 A9, which are U+00E9 in UTF-8 - the server used the file at that other name whenever one was there, which allows a local attacker who can create that file or its folder but cannot change the configured one, as any user can by default beside a file an administrator keeps under ProgramData, to have a port that logs on by client certificate (from 6.2.25) accept certificates from a certificate authority of the attacker's own and so sign in over the network as any mailbox without its password; to have the server trust such an authority for its object store and, intercepting that connection, read and modify the messages it stores; to receive the private keys the ACME client writes, the key of a certificate issued for the server's names among them; or to keep TLS ports from starting. The configuration is not the default: by default these files have names in ASCII, client certificates are off on every port, and the object store and ACME are off. The Linux builds are not affected.
